paper_title: Detecting Dark Matter with Superconducting Nanowires
notes: Headline new bound: solid blue 'Bound WSi' curve in Fig. 4 (dark photon absorption), the 95% C.L. limit placed by the 4.3 ng prototype WSi SNSPD with 0.8 eV threshold and 10^4 s exposure (no dark counts observed). Paper defines L supset -(kappa/2) F_munu F'^munu (Eq. for L_hidden) and reports kappa = kinetic mixing directly, so chi = kappa (not chi^2). Assumed DM density rho_DM = 0.3 GeV/cm^3 (Appendix); DM-search limit reported at paper's native density, not rescaled. Curve extracted from the vector PDF Plots/abs_HP_final.pdf via get_drawings: the pure-blue (RGB 0,0,1) width-3.0 stroke path, cross-checked against pure-blue raster pixels (median per column matched to <2%). Axes calibrated from tick strokes: x-axis log, majors 0.1/0.2/0.5/1/2 eV -> 470.3 px/decade; y-axis log, decade ticks anchored 10^-9 (y=108.98) to 10^-17 (y=644.8), 66.98 px/decade. Curve spans m_V ~ 0.84 eV (device 0.8 eV threshold) to 4.0 eV (right frame edge), kappa ~7e-9 down to ~3.8e-9, nearly flat and slowly declining with mass. A second, thinner blue vector path exists in the file at lower kappa but is entirely overpainted/clipped and not visible in the rendered figure; the visible headline curve is the width-3.0 path used here. Described in text as 'the strongest terrestrial constraint to date on dark photons with sub-eV masses.'
